Petnehaza Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Petneháza, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews settled in Petneháza in the late 19th century, peaking at 199 residents by 1890 before declining to 62 by 1941. Following 1869's Schism in Hungarian Jewry, the community joined the Orthodox stream, maintaining a synagogue, mikveh, and shochet, and joining Nyírmada's registrar jurisdiction by 1885. By 1944, only 44 Jews remained under Rabbi Samu Rosenbaum of Nyíregyháza; immediately after Passover that year, they were sent to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto and deported weeks later to Auschwitz. Ten survivors returned but did not stay long. This cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with tombstones through 1943.
